parts.title: Part 1
parts.instr: Listen to Owen and his aunt. For each question, tick the correct picture.

items.q: Where are the shopping bags?
whys: Aunt asks if they are in the car, and Owen says 'No, they aren't.'
Aunt asks about the bike basket, but Owen didn't bring his bike.
items.hint: Aunt guesses twice. Listen to what Owen says after 'No'.
items.worked: Owen says 'No, they aren't. They're in my backpack.'

stim.head: Listen to Owen and his aunt at the food market.
lines: Owen, are the shopping bags in the car?
No, they aren't. They're in my backpack.
Oh, good. Not in your bike basket?
No, I didn't bring my bike today.

items.q: Which bread does Owen want to buy?
whys: Aunt asks about a long loaf, but Owen says 'No, not a long one.'
Aunt asks about the square one for sandwiches. Owen says 'No'.
items.hint: Listen for what the bread LOOKS like. Which shape does Owen ask for?
items.worked: Owen asks for 'a round one with a hole in it', and then says 'the round one, please!'

stim.head: Listen to Owen and his aunt at the food market.
lines: Shall we get a long loaf of bread, Owen?
No, not a long one. Can we get a round one with a hole in it?
Not the square one for sandwiches?

items.q: What does Owen want to be when he is older?
whys: Aunt asks about being a fisherman, but Owen feels sick on boats.
Owen wanted to be a cook last year. Now he likes growing vegetables more.
items.hint: Two jobs are in the past or are only Aunt's idea. Which job does Owen want NOW?
items.worked: Owen says 'I want to be a farmer.' Now he likes growing vegetables.

stim.head: Listen to Owen and his aunt at the food market.
lines: Would you like to be a fisherman one day, Owen?
No, I feel sick on boats. I want to be a farmer.
Last year you wanted to be a cook!
Yes, but now I like growing vegetables more.

items.q: What is Owen going to have for lunch?
whys: Owen had noodles for breakfast, so he says 'No, thanks.'
Aunt says he loves sandwiches, but Owen says 'Not today.'
items.hint: Owen says 'No' to two foods. Which food does he ask for?
items.worked: Owen asks 'Can I have rice and fish?' and then says 'Rice and fish, please!'

stim.head: Listen to Owen and his aunt at the food market.
lines: Would you like some noodles for lunch, Owen?
No, thanks. I had noodles for breakfast. Can I have rice and fish?
Not a sandwich? You love sandwiches.
Not today. Rice and fish, please!

items.q: What time is Owen's dad going to come today?
whys: Twelve o'clock is when Dad usually comes on Saturday. Today is different.
One o'clock is when the market closes, not when Dad comes.
items.hint: Dad usually comes at one time, but today he is later. How much later?
items.worked: Dad usually comes at twelve o'clock. Today he is 'coming half an hour later', so he comes at half past twelve.

stim.head: Listen to Owen and his aunt at the food market.
lines: Is your dad coming at twelve o'clock, like every Saturday?
Not today. He's playing football, so he's coming half an hour later.
Good. The market closes at one o'clock, so we've got time for a drink!

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear each conversation twice.

items.q: You will hear two friends talking about a rainbow. What did Luna like most about it?
whys: Luna liked the bright colours, but she says something else was the best.
Seb says the size was the best part for him. That is Seb's idea, not Luna's.
items.hint: Listen for 'what I liked most'. Who says it?
items.worked: Luna says 'do you know what I liked most? There were two rainbows, one on top of the other!'

stim.head: You will hear two friends talking about a rainbow.
lines: Did you see the rainbow after school yesterday, Luna?
Yes! I saw it from the bus. The colours were so bright.
I liked the colours too, but the best part for me was the size. It went right over the park!
It was huge. But do you know what I liked most? There were two rainbows, one on top of the other!
Two? Really? I only saw one!

items.q: You will hear a girl and a boy talking about a karate class. Why is Tam starting karate?
whys: Tam's brother has the medals. Tam says he doesn't care about medals.
Emily guesses this, but Tam says 'Not really. I'm already strong.'
items.hint: Emily guesses two reasons. Is she right? Listen to what Tam says first.
items.worked: Tam says 'I'm a bit shy, so I want to feel braver. Dad says karate can help.'

stim.head: You will hear a girl and a boy talking about a karate class.
lines: Hi, Tam. Is that bag for your new karate class?
Yes! I'm a bit shy, so I want to feel braver. Dad says karate can help.
Oh! I thought it was because of your brother. He's got lots of karate medals.
He has, but I don't care about medals.
And you want to get stronger, don't you?

items.q: You will hear two friends talking about a lost scarf. Where do they agree to look first?
whys: Luna has already looked in the classroom. The scarf isn't there.
They will look on the field only if the scarf isn't in the box.
items.hint: Listen for 'first' and for 'Good idea'.
items.worked: Seb says 'Let's look in the lost property box first' and Luna says 'Good idea.'

stim.head: You will hear two friends talking about a lost scarf.
lines: Seb, I can't find my scarf. The blue one with stripes.
Did you leave it in the classroom?
No, I looked there. I took it off when we played football. So it's on the field, I think.
Let's look in the lost property box first. The caretaker puts everything there.
Good idea. If it isn't there, we can check the football field after that.

items.q: You will hear two friends talking about a class model of the planets. Which planet is Tam going to make?
whys: Tam wanted Saturn first, but Luna is already making it.
Emily says Mars, but Tam thinks it is too small. Emily makes Mars.
items.hint: Tam changes his mind. Listen for 'I'm going to make'.
items.worked: Tam says 'Mars is too small. I'm going to make Jupiter. It's the biggest.'

stim.head: You will hear two friends talking about a class model of the planets.
lines: Tam, which planet are you making for our class model?
First I wanted Saturn, because of the rings. But Luna's already making it.
So what about Mars? You've got lots of red paint.
Mars is too small. I'm going to make Jupiter. It's the biggest, and I can use an old football!
Great idea. Then I'll make Mars!

items.q: You will hear two friends talking about a pancake breakfast. What is Seb most interested in?
whys: Luna guesses this, but Seb says he is more interested in something else.
Luna is going to help her mum cook. Seb doesn't say he wants to help.
items.hint: Luna guesses first. Listen for 'I'm more interested in'.
items.worked: Seb says 'I like pancakes, but I'm more interested in the pancake race.'

stim.head: You will hear two friends talking about a pancake breakfast.
lines: Luna, are you going to the pancake breakfast at the sports club on Sunday?
Yes! My mum's making the pancakes. Are you going to eat lots of them?
Well, I like pancakes, but I'm more interested in the pancake race. People run and flip pancakes in a pan!
My dad's in the race! I'm going to help my mum cook.
Cool. I'll shout for your dad!

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instr: You will hear Nora talking to a cook about a junior cooking class. For each question, write the missing information.

items.q: Write the missing information for question 11.
items.hint: Two ages are said. Which one is Nora's age NOW?
items.worked: Nora says 'I'm eight.' She will be nine in March, so nine is not her age now.

stim.head:
JUNIOR COOKING CLASS
First name: Nora (example)
(11) Age: ________
(12) Address: 15 ________ Street
(13) Mum's phone number: ________
(14) Day of the class: ________
(15) Food Nora can't eat: ________
lines: Hello! Are you here for the junior cooking class?
Yes, please. I'd like to join.
Thank you, Nora. How old are you?
I'm eight. But I'll be nine in March!
So you're eight now. Good. And where do you live?
Thanks. Now, what's your mum's phone number?
It's zero nine eight three, six two seven, four one five.
Lovely. We have classes on Saturday and Sunday. Which day would you like?
I visit my grandma every Saturday, so Sunday, please.
Sunday. And is there any food you can't eat?
Sorry? Do you mean food I don't like?
No, I mean food that makes you ill.
Oh! Nuts make me ill. I can't eat nuts. But I love eggs and cheese!
OK, no nuts for you. See you on Sunday, Nora!

items.hint: Nora spells the street name. Write each letter you hear.

parts.title: Part 1
parts.instr: Look and read. For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.q: What does the sign ask you to do?
opts: Cover the sandpit when you finish playing.
Keep your cat away from the sandpit.
Play in the sandpit only when the lid is on.
whys: The sign talks about cats, but it doesn't ask you to keep your cat away.
You can't play in the sand with the lid on. The lid goes on AFTER you play.
items.hint: Read the sentence that starts with 'Please'. When does the lid go on?
items.worked: The sign says 'Please put the lid back on when you finish playing.' The lid covers the sandpit.

stim.head: Sign
stim.html:
SANDPIT
Please put the lid back on when you finish playing.
Cats like sand too! 🐈

items.q: Why did Mum write to Tam?
opts: to ask him to buy some food
to invite him to Grandma's house
to tell him what Grandma is cooking
whys: Grandma is coming to Tam's home. Tam isn't going to Grandma's house.
The message doesn't say what Grandma is cooking. Grandma is a visitor.
items.hint: Which sentence in the message asks Tam to do a job?
items.worked: Mum writes 'Please buy a little rice and a few eggs on your way home.'

stim.head: Text message
stim.html:
MESSAGE FROM MUM
Hi Tam! Grandma is coming for supper tonight. Please buy a little rice and a few eggs on your way home. Love, Mum

items.q: Why is this notice in the hotel rooms?
opts: The hotel wants to save energy.
The lights in the rooms are broken.
Guests must charge their phones in the rooms.
whys: The notice doesn't say the lights are broken. It asks you to turn them off.
The notice asks you to unplug your charger, not to charge your phone.
items.hint: Read the heading. What does 'Help our planet' tell you about the reason?
items.worked: The heading says 'HELP OUR PLANET'. Turning off lights and unplugging chargers saves energy.

stim.head: Notice
stim.html:
HILLTOP HOTEL: HELP OUR PLANET!
💡 Please turn off the lights and unplug your charger when you leave your room.

items.q: What does the table show?
opts: People bought fewer banana cakes than lemon cakes.
The lemon cake was the most popular cake.
More banana cakes were sold than chocolate cakes.
whys: Chocolate cake sold 21. That is more than lemon cake (14).
Banana cake sold 9 and chocolate cake sold 21. This is the wrong way round.
items.hint: Compare the numbers. Which number is the biggest? Which is the smallest?
items.worked: Banana cake sold 9 and lemon cake sold 14. 9 is fewer than 14.

stim.head: Table
stim.html:
SPORTS CLUB BAKE SALE
CakeNumber sold
Lemon cake14
Chocolate cake21
Banana cake9

items.q: What should visitors do?
opts: Knock on the door and not ring the bell.
Ring the bell and wait for the baby.
Come back when the baby wakes up.
whys: The sign says 'Don't ring the bell.'
The sign doesn't ask visitors to come back later. It tells them how to call.
items.hint: Read the two short sentences. One says 'do' and one says 'don't'.
items.worked: The sign says 'Please knock. Don't ring the bell.'

stim.head: Sign on a front door
stim.html:
SHH! BABY SLEEPING 👶
Please knock. Don't ring the bell.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instr: For each question, choose the best reply.

items.q: "Would you like some of my popcorn?"
opts: No, thanks. I've already had some.
No, thanks. I haven't had any yet.
Yes, please. I never eat popcorn.
whys: If you haven't had any yet, why say 'No, thanks'? This doesn't make sense.
If you never eat popcorn, you would not say 'Yes, please'.
items.hint: Read the whole reply. Do the two parts make sense together?
items.worked: 'No, thanks. I've *already* had some.' You say no because you ate some before.

items.q: "What would you like to do in the school holidays?"
opts: I'd like to visit my cousins.
I visited my cousins last summer.
My cousins live near the sea.
whys: The question is about the coming holidays, but this answer is about last summer.
This answer says where your cousins live. The question asks what you want to do.
items.hint: Look at 'would like to do'. Which reply uses the same pattern?
items.worked: 'What would you *like to do*?' → 'I'd *like to visit* my cousins.'

items.q: "Why are you going to the library?"
opts: To find a book about planets.
It's next to the sports centre.
whys: This answer says when and who, not why.
This answer says where the library is, not why you are going.
items.hint: The question word is 'Why'. Which reply gives a reason with 'to + verb'?
items.worked: 'Why are you going?' → '*To find* a book about planets.' To + verb gives the reason.

items.q: "I can't find my kitten anywhere!"
opts: Don't worry. She might be in the garden.
Don't worry. She had to go in the garden.
Really? I've got a kitten too.
whys: 'Had to' means someone made her go. Nobody knows where the kitten is.
This reply doesn't help your friend with the problem.
items.hint: Your friend is worried. Which reply gives a possible place?
items.worked: 'She *might* be in the garden.' We use 'might' when we are not sure.

items.q: "Who reads more carefully, you or your brother?"
opts: My brother does. He reads more carefully than me.
My brother does. He reads more quickly than me.
Yes, he does. He reads very carefully.
whys: The question is about reading carefully, not quickly.
'Who' questions don't have a yes or no answer.
items.hint: Look at the question word 'Who' and the word 'carefully'.
items.worked: 'Who reads *more carefully*?' → 'My brother does. He reads *more carefully* than me.'

items.q: "I've got a bad cold and a sore throat."
opts: Oh dear! Drink some warm water and rest.
Oh dear! Don't stay at home today.
Great! Let's go swimming after school.
whys: When you are ill, you should stay at home and rest.
Your friend is ill. 'Great!' is not a kind reply, and swimming is not good for a cold.
items.hint: Your friend is ill. Which reply gives good advice?
items.worked: '*Drink* some warm water and *rest*.' The imperatives give good advice to someone who is ill.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct word.

items.q: The moon looks really bright tonight, ________?
whys: The verb is 'looks', not 'is'. 'Looks' needs 'does' in the tag.
The sentence is positive, so the tag must be negative.
items.hint: Find the verb. Is the sentence positive or negative?
items.worked: 'The moon *looks*' is positive present simple, so the tag is '*doesn't it*?'

items.q: You haven't seen my blue pencil case, ________?
whys: The sentence is already negative (haven't), so the tag must be positive.
The verb is 'haven't seen', so the tag uses 'have', not 'did'.
items.hint: The sentence is negative. Which helping verb does it use?
items.worked: 'You *haven't* seen ...' is negative, so the tag is positive: '*have you*?'

items.q: Please put a ________ salt on my boiled egg.
whys: 'A few' is for things you can count, like 'a few eggs'. You can't count salt.
'Many' is for things you can count. Also, we don't say 'a many'.
items.hint: Can you count salt? Then choose the word for things you can't count.
items.worked: We can't count salt, so we say '*a little* salt'.

items.q: I looked in the fridge, but there wasn't ________ to eat.
whys: We use 'something' in positive sentences. This sentence has 'wasn't'.
'Wasn't' is already negative. We don't say 'wasn't nothing'.
items.hint: Look for 'not' or 'n't' in the sentence.
items.worked: 'There *wasn't anything*.' We use 'anything' after a negative verb.

items.q: Rinse the cress seeds, ________ put them on wet cotton wool.
whys: 'While' needs a person and a verb after it, like 'while you wait'.
'When' needs a person and a verb after it, like 'when you finish'.
items.hint: These are two instructions in order. Which word can come straight before an instruction like 'put'?
items.worked: 'Rinse the seeds, *then* put them on wet cotton wool.' 'Then' joins two steps in order.

items.q: My little sister really enjoys ________ in puddles.
whys: After 'enjoy' we use -ing, not 'to' + verb.
After 'enjoy' we need the -ing form of the verb.
items.hint: Which form comes after 'enjoy'?
items.worked: We say 'enjoy + -ing': she *enjoys jumping*.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instr: Read Vinh's story about a class trip. For each question, choose the correct word. There is one example (0).

items.q: Gap (18): She showed us ________ cacao trees with big yellow pods.
whys: 'A little' is for things you can't count. You can count trees.
'Much' is for things you can't count, like 'much water'.
items.hint: Can you count trees? Choose the word for countable nouns.
items.worked: 'Trees' is a plural countable noun, so we say '*a few* cacao trees'.

stim.head: A class trip
stim.html:
Our Trip to a Cacao Farm
by Vinh, Class 3C

Last Friday, our class visited a cacao farm outside the city. (0) Every child wore a sun hat, because the day was very hot.

The farmer met us at the gate. She showed us (18) ________ cacao trees with big yellow pods. She cut one pod open (19) ________ us the beans inside. The beans were white and sticky!

Next, we went into the farm kitchen. We (20) ________ wash our hands before we touched anything, because that is the rule in the kitchen.

(21) ________ the farmer roasted the beans, the whole room smelled of chocolate. Then we crushed the beans to make a paste. I crushed my beans (22) ________ than my friends, so my paste was very smooth.

At the end, the farmer gave each of us (23) ________ special to take home. It was a small bar of chocolate with vanilla in it!

I have (24) ________ eaten half of my bar. I'm keeping the rest for my mum. I hope to visit the farm again next year!

items.q: Gap (19): She cut one pod open ________ us the beans inside.
whys: We need a reason here: WHY did she cut the pod open? Use 'to + verb'.
We can't put two verbs together like 'cut ... show'. Use 'to + verb' for a reason.
items.hint: Ask 'Why did she cut it open?' Which answer gives the reason?
items.worked: She cut the pod open *to show* us the beans. 'To + verb' tells us why.

'Could' means it was possible. A rule is something you must do.
items.hint: Read to the end of the sentence. Is washing hands a rule or just a possibility?
items.worked: The text says 'because that is the rule', so we use '*had to*' for something we must do.

Last Friday, our class visited a cacao farm outside the city. (0) Every child wore a sun hat, because the day was very hot.

The farmer met us at the gate. She showed us (18) ________ cacao trees with big yellow pods. She cut one pod open (19) ________ us the beans inside. The beans were white and sticky!

Next, we went into the farm kitchen. We (20) ________ wash our hands before we touched anything, because that is the rule in the kitchen.

(21) ________ the farmer roasted the beans, the whole room smelled of chocolate. Then we crushed the beans to make a paste. I crushed my beans (22) ________ than my friends, so my paste was very smooth.

At the end, the farmer gave each of us (23) ________ special to take home. It was a small bar of chocolate with vanilla in it!

I have (24) ________ eaten half of my bar. I'm keeping the rest for my mum. I hope to visit the farm again next year!

items.q: Gap (23): At the end, the farmer gave each of us ________ special to take home.
whys: We use 'anything' in questions and negative sentences. This sentence is positive.
Read the next sentence. She gave them a chocolate bar, so she didn't give them nothing.
items.hint: Read the NEXT sentence. Did the children get a present?
items.worked: The next sentence says 'It was a small bar of chocolate', so she gave them *something* special.

parts.title: Part 5
parts.instr: Read what three children say about their favourite breakfast. For each question, choose the correct name.

items.q: Who enjoys something about the place where they eat breakfast?
whys: Yusuf talks about the kitchen, but he doesn't say he enjoys being there.
Matilda has a clock on the kitchen table, but she doesn't say she enjoys the kitchen.
items.hint: Find WHERE each child eats. Who says they love something there?
items.worked: Chi eats on the balcony and says 'I love watching the birds in the tree next to it.'

stim.head: Three children
stim.html:
My favourite breakfast

Chi
My favourite breakfast is sticky rice with mango. My grandma makes it for me every Sunday. We eat it on the balcony of our flat, and I love watching the birds in the tree next to it. On school days, I have to eat quickly, so I just have a banana. I never want to change my Sunday breakfast. It's perfect!

Yusuf
I love eggs for breakfast. My dad can cook them in lots of ways, but my favourite is a cheese omelette. On Saturdays, I help my dad to cook. I have to be careful, because the pan gets very hot. I think a hot breakfast is better than a cold one. It keeps me full until lunch, so I'm never hungry in class.

Matilda
I usually have cereal with milk for breakfast, but I'm bored of it now. I'd like to try something new, like papaya with yoghurt. My cousin eats that every day. My school bus comes at seven o'clock, so I haven't got much time. Mum puts a little clock on the kitchen table. It helps me to eat fast and not miss the bus!

items.q: Who has to be careful sometimes?
whys: Chi says 'I have to eat quickly'. That is about time, not being careful.
Matilda has to be fast for the bus. She doesn't say she must be careful.
items.hint: Two children say 'have to'. Read what comes after it.
items.worked: Yusuf cooks with his dad and says 'I have to be careful, because the pan gets very hot.'

parts.title: Part 6
parts.instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.q: Why did Emily talk to her mum?
opts: Things that could be recycled were in the bins.
The big bins downstairs were too small.
She wanted her mum to clean the bins.
whys: The bins were full, but the article doesn't say they were too small.
Emily and her mum made a plan. Nobody cleaned the bins.
items.hint: Read the first two paragraphs. What problem did Emily notice?
items.worked: The bins were full of bottles, newspapers and tins, and 'Emily knew that lots of these things could be recycled.'

stim.head: Article
stim.html:
Emily's Green Team

Emily is eight years old. She lives on the sixth floor of a tall block of flats. Last spring, she noticed a problem. Every week, the big bins downstairs were full of plastic bottles, old newspapers and empty tins.

Emily knew that lots of these things could be recycled. She talked to her mum, and together they made a plan.

First, Emily made a colourful poster and put it next to the lift. It asked every family to come to a meeting on Saturday. Emily was worried that only a few people would come. But on Saturday, eighteen neighbours arrived, and some of them brought biscuits!

At the meeting, everyone agreed to start a recycling club. Now there are three big boxes on the ground floor: one for paper, one for plastic and one for tins. Every Friday, Emily and two older children check the boxes.

The club has already collected more than five hundred bottles. Each month, a man from the recycling centre takes everything away. He gives the club a little money for it.

'Our roof is grey and empty,' says Emily. 'We want to use the money to buy plants. Then it can be a garden for everyone!'

items.q: What can we understand about the meeting?
opts: More people came than Emily expected.
Only a few neighbours came to the meeting.
whys: Emily was worried about this, but eighteen neighbours came.
Some neighbours brought biscuits. Emily didn't make them.
items.hint: Emily was worried before the meeting. Then read what happened on Saturday.
items.worked: Emily 'was worried that only a few people would come', but 'eighteen neighbours arrived'.

items.worked: The text says 'Every Friday, Emily and two older children check the boxes.' Every Friday is once a week.

tasks.title: My best friend
tasks.prompt: Write about your best friend. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: What is he or she like?
Why is this person special to you?
starters: He / She is special to me because ...

models.text: My best friend is a girl in my class. she is kind and funny. She like drawing pictures. We play football at break time. she is special because she always help me
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four questions are answered, but the reason is very short (help me with what?).
Organisation and layout 1/2: one paragraph in a sensible order, but only 'and' and 'because' link the ideas.
Grammar 1/2: simple sentences, but two verb mistakes: 'she like' should be 'she likes' and 'she always help' should be 'she always helps'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: words are spelt correctly, but they are simple (kind, funny). The answer is a little short.
Writing conventions 1/2: two sentences start without a capital letter ('she'), and the last sentence has no full stop.

models.text: My best friend lives next door to me. He is tall and very funny, and he has short black hair. Every afternoon, we ride our bikes in our street. At the weekend, we play board games together. He is special to me because he always makes me laugh. I like him a lot.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four questions are answered, with a clear reason ('he always makes me laugh').
Organisation and layout 1/2: one paragraph in a good order, but the linking words are limited ('and', 'because').
Grammar 2/2: present simple is correct all through ('lives', 'has', 'makes'), with some time phrases at the start of sentences.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: correct spelling and some describing words (tall, funny, short black hair), but 'like' and 'a lot' are a little plain.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: My best friend sits next to me in class. She is small and cheerful, and she has long curly hair. She is very clever, but she is never bossy. After school, we often play badminton, and then we do our homework together. She is special to me because she listens when I feel sad.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four questions are answered with details, and the reason is clear and personal.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one paragraph in a logical order, with a range of linking words (and, but, after school, then, because, when).
Grammar 2/2: accurate present simple, adverbs of frequency ('often', 'never') and a 'when' clause.
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied describing words (cheerful, curly, clever, bossy), all spelt correctly.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with correct capital letters, commas and full stops.

tasks.title: A park or playground near my home
tasks.prompt: Write about a park or playground in your neighbourhood. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: What is it and where is it?
What is one special thing there, and what do people use it for?
starters: There is a ... near my home.
The best thing is ... People use it to ...

models.text: There is a park near my flat. it is big and green. There is a lake in the park. People goes there for fishing. I like the park becaus i can play with my friends.
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four questions are touched on, but there are few details about what the park looks like.
Organisation and layout 1/2: one paragraph in a sensible order, but most sentences are not linked.
Grammar 1/2: simple sentences, with one verb mistake ('People goes' should be 'People go'). There is no 'to + verb' for the use.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: simple words (big, green) and one spelling mistake: 'becaus' should be 'because'. A little short.
Writing conventions 1/2: the sentences are complete, but 'it' and 'i' need capital letters.

models.text: There is a small playground behind my block of flats. It has green grass, two swings and a red slide. There is also a big sandpit. Children use it to build sandcastles. I go there every afternoon with my little brother. I like it because it is near my home and it is fun.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four questions are answered: where it is, what it looks like, the sandpit and why the writer likes it.
Organisation and layout 1/2: one paragraph in a clear order, but 'and' is used a lot and there are few other linking words.
Grammar 2/2: correct present simple, 'There is' and 'It has', and 'to + verb' for the use ('to build sandcastles').
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: correct spelling, but the describing words are simple (small, big, red, fun).
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: My favourite place is Lotus Park, near my school. It is wide and quiet, with tall trees and a small lake in the middle. The best thing is the long wooden bridge. People walk across it to feed the ducks. In the evening, my family goes there to relax. I love this park because it is peaceful, and I always feel happy there.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four questions are answered with good details, and the reason is developed ('peaceful', 'I always feel happy').
Organisation and layout 2/2: one paragraph in a logical order, with linking words and time phrases (and, with, in the evening, because).
Grammar 2/2: accurate present simple, 'with' phrases for describing, and two 'to + verb' uses ('to feed', 'to relax').
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied, topic words (wide, quiet, wooden bridge, peaceful), all spelt correctly.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with correct capital letters, commas and full stops.
